titleStmt.title: A Two-level Hierarchical Scheduling Scheme for Hybrid Tasks in Priority-Based Preemptive Systems

analytic.title: A Two-level Hierarchical Scheduling Scheme for Hybrid Tasks in Priority-Based Preemptive Systems

div.p: For the application of hybrid tasks in priority-based preemptive systems, an innovative two-level hierarchical scheduling scheme is presented, and the time-triggered mode and event-triggered mode are adopted for the periodic real-time tasks and aperiodic real-time tasks respectively. First, the scheduling structure is proposed and the related concepts are defined. Then, the task model is established, and some crucial technologies such as scheduling algorithm, schedulability and jitter control are deeply researched. Subsequently, combined with Windows CE.NET, the experiment validation of scheduling scheme is carried out and the results demonstrate that the method can improve the determination of real-time tasks and reduce jitter. Specially, the jitter can be even eliminated if the task periods and tick-interval are rational. Finally, the choice of tick-interval is discussed. So the proposed scheduling scheme is efficient for hybrid tasks.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: The theoretical research on scheduling algorithms for real-time systems has been a crucial question all the time. The essence of scheduling algorithm is to determine the task execution in a given task set and resources in order to meet task deadline. In 1973, Rate Monotonic (RM) and Earliest Deadline First (EDF) algorithms are proposed by Liu and Layland [1]. RM and EDF are the most classical scheduling algorithms in real-time applications, and a lot of real-time algorithms are based on RM and EDF later.

In recent years, the domains of real-time systems applications have broadened from the primary periodic real-time tasks (PRTT) to hybrid tasks (HT) composed of PRTT, aperiodic real-time tasks (ARTT) and non real-time tasks (NRTT). Therefore, the scheduling of hybrid tasks is gradually drew attention and many related scheduling algorithms are proposed. One kind is server-based scheduling such as DS (Deferrable Server), SS (Sporadic Server), PE (Priority Exchange), MS (Multiple Server), etc.; another kind is bandwidth reservation-based server scheduling such as total bandwith server, constant bandwith server, etc [2]. The above-mentioned scheduling algorithms are to guarantee the periodic task executions firstly and reserve some Manuscript received October 1, 2007. processor resources for the aperiodic tasks. In addition, Z Deng, JWS Liu, etc. put forward a two-level hierarchical scheduling scheme from the view of the scheduling structure, which is realized by embedding a layer scheduling module that adopts RM, EDF, fixed-priority, etc [3][4]. At the same time, combined with operating system (OS) scheduler, the task priority is altered through static or dynamic mode and thus to achieve the real-time applications. But the uncertain factors caused by the two-level scheduling and HT may result in the inacceptable jitter for real-time applications.

In order to improve the determination of real-time tasks and reduce jitter, this paper presents an innovative two-level hierarchical scheduling scheme, which is realized through the time-triggered and event-triggered (TT-ET) mode. The schedulability and jitter control are deeply analyzed, and then the feasibility of scheduling scheme is validated via Windows CENET platform.

div.head: II. TWO-LEVEL HIERARCHICAL SCHEDULING SCHEME
div.p: BASED ON TT-ET

In practical applications, especially in the field of industrial control, the user's behavior, the status change of input signal and the communication between the inner modules may trigger an event, and generally the event is processed with event-triggered mode. As to the periodic sampling control, output controls, etc., the superiority is obvious if the time-triggered mode is adopted [5][6]. So it is a significant trend that the mixed control systems based TT-ET is researched.

The aperiodic event-triggered thread (ETT) is generally processed through priority scheduling, and the static round-robin scheduling is chose for time-triggered thread (TTT). This section presents an innovative two-level hierarchical scheduling scheme based on TT-ET, and some related technologies such as scheduling algorithms and schedulability are deeply analyzed.

A. Scheduling Structure The two-level hierarchical scheduling structure is shown in Fig 1. The priority of NRTT is lower than the priority of PRTT and ARTT, so a time-sharing scheduling algorithm is adopted for NRTT after the real-time tasks are finished or blocked. To a great extent, the average response time of NRTT is affected by real-time task executions. For PRTT set, PRTT are regularly running in the TTT through time-trigger scheduling algorithm; however, for ARTT set, they are finished in ETT. In addition, it is necessary that the schedulability analyses of real-time tasks are carried out before they enter the ready queues in order to ensure the real-time performance. HTset. div.head: III. THE VALIDATION OF SCHEDULING SCHEME
div.p: For the above-mentioned scheduling scheme, combined with Windows CE.NET OS platform, the scheduling algorithm is validated in this section.

A. Windows CE. NET scheduling algorithm Windows CE uses a priority-based time-slice (lOOms) algorithm to schedule the execution of threads. A thread can have one of the 256 priorities. The top 249 (O through 248) priorities are real-time priority levels. The bottom eight (248 through 255) priorities are non-real-time priority levels. Threads with a higher priority run first. Threads with the same priority run in a round-robin fashion when a thread has stopped running, all other threads of the same priority run before the original thread can continue. Threads at a lower priority do not run until all threads with a higher priority have either finished or have been blocked. If one thread is running and a thread of higher priority is unblocked, the lower-priority thread is immediately suspended and the higher-priority thread is scheduled [ 10].

div.head: V. CONCLUSIONS
div.p: In this paper, we presented a two-level hierarchical scheduling scheme based on TT-ET for real-time applications. Then according to task characteristic, the schedulability and jitter control analyses are provided. The scheduling scheme presented is realized and tested through Windows CE.NET platform, and the results testify that the scheduling algorithm is more efficient for priority-based preemptive systems. If HT is schedulable, ARTT can be responded in time too.
